full_caption: Verdant Acre Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellant, v. Horatio Oakhampton, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: The parties own adjoining parcels on Mill Race Way. The dispute concerns a strip approximately 25 feet in width lying between the fence line maintained since 1983 and the line described in the parties' respective deeds.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Horatio Oakhampton had constructive notice of the disputed occupation. Possession that is open and visible puts a purchaser on inquiry as to the rights of the possessor, and a purchaser who fails to inquire is charged with what inquiry would have disclosed.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The doctrine of acquiescence establishes a boundary where adjoining owners have recognized and treated a visible line as the boundary for the statutory period, regardless of what the deeds provide.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Where a deed description conflicts with monuments actually set on the ground, the monuments control. Calls in a conveyance are given priority in the order: natural monuments, artificial monuments, courses, distances, and quantity.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: A quiet-title plaintiff must recover on the strength of its own title and not on the weakness of the defendant's. Verdant Acre Capital Servicing, LLC traced an unbroken chain to the 2004 patent and thereby carried that burden as to the residue of the parcel.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The fence erected in 1983 was maintained jointly, and both households mowed to their respective sides without objection until Verdant Acre Capital Servicing, LLC obtained the 1988 survey. That course of conduct satisfies the acquiescence standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A retracement that ignores an original monument capable of being located is entitled to little weight. We accept the trial court's finding crediting the monument-based survey.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Acquiescence requires (1) occupation up to a visible line, (2) mutual recognition of that line as the boundary, and (3) continuance for 20 years. Silence coupled with occupation may supply the element of mutual recognition.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The recording act of this State is a race-notice statute. A subsequent purchaser for value prevails over a prior unrecorded interest only if the purchaser took without notice and recorded first.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The surveyor called by Verdant Acre Capital Servicing, LLC located the original iron pin at the southeast corner and retraced the line from that monument. The surveyor called by Horatio Oakhampton began from a subdivision plat computation without locating any original monument.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The judgment quieting title in Verdant Acre Capital Servicing, LLC to the disputed strip is affirmed. The counterclaim for trespass damages is remanded for a determination of the value of the removed timber.

sections.heading: RIDER I — BOUNDARY LINE AGREEMENT
sections.text: The parties, being uncertain as to the true location of their common boundary, agree that the line established by the existing fence, as located and monumented by the survey of record dated January 27, 2010, is and shall be the boundary between their respective parcels for all purposes. Each party quitclaims to the other all right, title and interest lying on the other's side of the agreed line. This agreement shall be recorded and shall bind the parties' successors.

sections.heading: RIDER II — SURVEY AND MONUMENTATION
sections.text: The agreed line shall be monumented with iron pins set at each angle point and at intervals not exceeding 25 feet, and a plat of the survey shall be filed with the Rooksbury County Recorder. In the event of conflict between this description and the monuments as set, the monuments shall control.

sections.heading: RIDER III — TITLE WARRANTIES AND EXCEPTIONS
sections.text: The conveyance is made subject to: (a) all easements, restrictions and reservations of record; (b) the rights of parties in possession as disclosed by an accurate survey; (c) real property taxes for the current year, prorated as of closing; and (d) the encroachment of the retaining wall across the common line as shown on the survey. Grantor's warranty of title excepts each of the foregoing.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Force Majeure
sections.text: Neither party shall be liable for a failure of performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an act of God, flood, fire, civil disturbance, governmental order, epidemic, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control, provided the affected party gives notice within 7 days and resumes performance as promptly as practicable.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Kestrel.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.
